question.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying the equation through by $9$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2t & =\frac{4-6t}{9} \\ \frac{4-6t}{9} & =-2t \\ 9(\frac{4-6t}{9}) & =9(-2t) \\ \cancel{9}(\frac{4-6t}{\cancel{9}}) & =-18t \\ 4-6t & =-18t\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}4-6t & =-18t \\ 4-6t+6t & =-18t+6t \\ 4 & =-12t \\ -12t & =4 \\ \frac{-12t}{-12} & =\frac{4}{-12} \\ \frac{\cancel{-12}t}{\cancel{-12}} & =-\frac{1}{3} \\ t & =-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
